subject: Recap: selection playbook & next tests (Redwood demo)
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Holly Burns <h.burns@medsync.com>, Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@medsync.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Aug 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: selection playbook & next tests (Redwood demo)

Holly / Daniel — thanks for the time today. Quick recap of what we covered, the goals you shared, and proposed next steps so we all have the same picture.

Key customer pain points (as discussed)
- Latency spikes on peak inference for interactive triage workflows (95th pct > 400ms).
- Unit cost for generation is unpredictable when traffic varies across cohorts.
- Need for a private deployment option for PHI data routing and auditability.

Stated goals
1) Consistent sub-200ms 95th percentile for the retrieval+generate path for 512-token prompts.
2) Predictable monthly unit cost within a 15% variance window.
3) A compliance-ready deployment option (VPC + KMS) for production sensitive flows.

Decision criteria (agreed on call)
- Performance: 95th latency, cold-start behavior.
- Reliability: fallbacks / graceful degradation.
- Cost: token/unit economics and reserved capacity options.
- Security: VPC, KMS, audit logs, SOC2 evidence.
- Ops: observability (per-route metrics, token-level cost breakdown).

Proposed validation plan (short timeline)
1) Sandbox latency sweep (Redwood to run): run 50k synthetic requests representative of your traffic mix, capture 50/95/99 latency and NVTX traces. Owner: Soojin. ETA: Aug 17 window.
2) Cost projection workbook: run existing traffic profile through quantized vs FP model variants and reserved capacity scenarios. Owner: Logan. Deliverable: selection-matrix.xlsx (attached). ETA: Aug 19.
3) Security checklist & evidence pack: example VPC design and KMS flow + SOC2 artifacts. Owner: Camila. Deliverable: redwood-demo-config.yaml (attached) + brief runbook. ETA: Aug 20.
4) Live POC week (if the metrics look good): run a 3-day POC with a pilot cohort, monitor quality regressions and cost. Decision gate: acceptance criteria above.

Open questions we left on the call
- Which of your user cohorts must remain on-prem vs can go to a cloud-hosted private deployment?
- What are expected peak concurrent sessions during weekdays?
- Any regulatory deadlines for audit evidence or contractual clauses we should know about?

Immediate asks for your team
- Please confirm the pilot cohort (size and data residency requirement).
- Send the sample prompt set (anonymized) you want us to use for the latency sweep.

I attached the selection matrix and a sample config file we’ll use for the sandbox. If you’re good with the plan I’ll schedule the latency sweep for Aug 17 and loop in Logan & Camila for the cost/security runs.

Thanks again — talk soon.

—
Soojin Lee
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0147

Attachments: redwood-demo-config.yaml (text), selection-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Thanks Soojin — this is great and aligns with what we need. A couple quick clarifications before you run the sweep: 

1) Data residency: the pilot cohort must stay in our US cloud region (no EU routing).
2) Latency SLO: our internal target is sub-200ms 95th for the full retrieval + generation path; if we can meet that in the sandbox it’s a strong signal.

We’ll send an anonymized prompt set by EOD tomorrow. Also — can you confirm whether the sandbox run will exercise your KV/prefix cache behavior (we saw cache misses on previous tests)?

—
Holly Burns
VP Product | MedSync Health
h.burns@medsync.com

Holly — great questions. Short answers below and a tiny bit more detail on the sweep so expectations are clear.

Data residency
- Sandbox and POC will be pinned to the US West region and will not route through EU. We will share the VPC subnet ranges and egress controls before the sweep.

Cache behavior
- The latency sweep will include cold-start runs and warmed-cache runs. We’ll run an initial 10k series to populate prefix/KV caches and then the main 50k sweep that alternates hot/cold to reproduce realistic hit/miss ratios. We’ll capture per-request KV hit/miss and include that in the report.

Schedule
- Proposed window for the sweep: Tue Aug 17, 09:00–13:00 PT. I’ll attach a test schedule (ICS) — please confirm if that works for your ops window.

Next steps I’ll take now
- Lock in the Aug 17 window (pending your confirmation).
- Spin up the sandbox config (redwood-demo-config.yaml) and post the endpoint and short-run health check results.

If that all looks good I’ll flag Logan to start the cost projection run in parallel.

—
Soojin Lee
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0147

Attachments: test-schedule.ics (calendar)

Team — internal note after the MedSync thread (forwarded below). High-level guidance and immediate asks before the sweep on Aug 17 (schedule confirmed with the customer).

Quick situational summary- MedSync has a clear latency-first bar for their interactive product. Security is table-stakes (they expect VPC + KMS + audit logs). They’re also very sensitive to cost variability; procurement will ask for committed pricing scenarios.

Competitive snapshot (what I heard / probe):
- Competitor A (closed-source): claims 150ms 95th but no public SOC2; pricing opaque; lacks per-route cost telemetry.
- Competitor B (open model provider): good token economics at high volume but higher tail latency on our initial tests (they use smaller batch sizes by default).

Immediate internal asks
- Camila: please prepare the minimal SOC2 evidence packet and a short VPC runbook we can share if they request it (focus on audit trails). Owner: Camila. ETA: EOD Aug 20.
- Logan: build the cost-scenarios in the attached selection-matrix.xlsx and include a reserved-capacity vs on-demand comparison for their traffic profile. Owner: Logan. ETA: Aug 19.
- I’ll run the latency sweep and surface per-route KV hit/miss metrics + trace artifacts.

Testing notes for the sweep (quick)
- Warm/cold alternation: 10k warm priming then 50k mixed-run.
- Capture 50/95/99, tail traces, per-token cost, KV hit ratio, and memory/GPU metrics.
- Export an artifacts bundle (zip) with traces and a short readme for how to reproduce.

If either of you disagree on owners or ETA, reply-all and we’ll adjust. I’ll pull the artifacts into the HubSpot record and the shared Drive link after the sweep.

Thanks —
Soojin
